title: Capture app errors to the database
description: Global window error and unhandledrejection handler, error boundary reporting, and the existing logError path, all writing through the deduplicating upsert from the signals backend task. Tag each error with the environment (local, staging, production). Depends on: Signals backend task. Result: merged in PR #28 (src/features/error-reporting; live on production).

title: Signals backend: error logs, feedback and bugs tables
description: Add supabase/migrations with error_logs (clustered by hash, upsert_error_log function), app_feedback and bugs tables, RLS, and a db:push-staging script, so the signal adapter in .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/signal-adapter.md has data to read. Forks get this by default. Admin = a role claim in the user's auth app_metadata (never user_metadata, which users can edit); admins and local dev can read, signed-in users can insert their own rows. Test it on a scratch Postgres, then apply it to the project; with isolated staging, staging first and production after merge. Result: merged in PR #27 (tables, upsert_error_log, RLS; Google sign-in and production build verified; one shared Supabase project by default, D10).

title: Onboarding states requirements, not methods
description: Rewrite the onboarding gates and the seeded Supabase and hosting tasks so they state setup requirements (end state, why, how the agent verifies, who acts) instead of vendor click paths, and add the staging Supabase project requirement. Decisions: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § onboarding-requirements. Result: merged in PR #26 (onboarding.md states requirements; Supabase and hosting requirement tables; signals epic queued).

title: Run the loop skill evals against the v0.42.0 baseline
description: Deferred from the skill-loop rework (skill-loop D59) to save usage. Run the eval cases under .agents/skills/router/evals/ and .agents/skills/loop-*/evals/ (15 cases), once with the new skill and once with the v0.42.0 skills it replaced (baseline = commit a920c0d), using the skill-creator workflow or `claude plugin eval`. Report pass rates per skill, and fix the skills where the new version loses behavior. Context: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § skill-loop. Result: 45/45 graders passed on new skills vs 39/45 on v0.42.0 baseline (composer-2.5); 0 regressions.

title: Show the harness overview on the app's home page and README
description: Publish the designed harness flowchart as an app route (/harness) built from kit components and the bronze theme tokens, with a PNG preview (public/harness-overview.png). Show a welcome card on the home page so visitors on the preview URL and on a fresh first run see it, and put the image at the top of README.md so people arriving from GitHub or Google see it. Result: merged in PR #32 (src/features/harness-overview, route /harness, public/harness-overview.png).

title: Fix Google sign-in returning to the wrong site with a PKCE error
description: Seen on the production site after signing in with Google from a preview: 'PKCE code verifier not found in storage'. Supabase auth logs show the sign-in started on the preview origin, Supabase redirected to the Site URL (production) because the app's bare-origin redirect address did not match the '/**' allow-list pattern, and production then failed with bad_code_verifier. The app also exchanges the code twice (supabase-js does it during client init, then the callback hook again), which would show a false error even when sign-in works. Decisions: documentation/DOC_DECISION_LOG.md § google-signin-return. Result: merged in PR #29 (0817eac, fix(auth): return Google sign-in to the app root and skip a redundant code exchange).

title: Define app vision
description: Collaborate with the coding agent to fill documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md (problem, persona, app role). Replace placeholder bullets with real prose and change Vision status from DRAFT to ACTIVE when complete. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § App vision & goals gate. Status: drafted by the agent from the Point At concept (2026-11-02); waiting for the owner to confirm and switch DRAFT to ACTIVE. Result: documentation/DOC_APP_VISION.md is ACTIVE; owner confirmed by merging value-machine/Fractal-tasks#1 (2026-11-04).

title: Put your app online (Cloudflare hosting)
description: Get your app live on the internet with Cloudflare (free tier is fine). Your coding agent does the setup — just ask it to "do the hosting task". What you need ready: a Cloudflare account, your Supabase keys already in .env, and (optional) a domain name you own. How it works once set up depends on your git workflow mode (see .claude/rules/git-workflow.md § Mode behavior table, rows staging and production) — by default every pull request gets its own preview link and merging the pull request ships to production. One step happens in the Cloudflare website (connecting your repo); the agent tells you what must be set there and why, waits for you, and checks the result. Agent playbook + troubleshooting: documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md (see "Agent one-shot brief"). If you explicitly say this app does not use Cloudflare, the agent offers to delete that hosting code (there is then no preview link). Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Hosting). Result (2026-11-06): Worker fractal-tasks on Cloudflare Workers Builds (account fabd04fbc9a4e48df759c76fc77399f7), production https://fractal-tasks.tom-fab.workers.dev from main, previews on all branches; build variables CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (build, not runtime, set on both the Production and the Previews tab; preview builds read only the Previews tab, so without it every preview shows "Supabase is not configured"). Verified: the live site loads /assets/*.js and shows the tree from the point-at function.

title: Decide whether the app uses anonymous sign-ins
description: The app asks Supabase for an anonymous session on every visit and Supabase refuses (anonymous_provider_disabled, HTTP 422), twice per page load. Either enable anonymous sign-ins in the project (anonymous users get the authenticated role, so the feedback policy would admit them; review RLS first) or remove the call. Auth permission model: needs an owner decision. Result (2026-11-06): owner chose to remove it; the app no longer calls signInAnonymously, so the 422s on every visit are gone.

title: Run the Point At first tests
description: Run the proposed first tests in documentation/DOC_POINT_AT_RISKS.md (sandwich, awkward task, mid-tree entry, adversarial plan, human leaf) against the deployed MCP server with real agents, and record results in the process change log. Result (2026-11-06): all five pass with friction; five bugs fixed and deployed; results in documentation/jobs/temp_job_first-tests/RESULTS.md.

title: Leaf dependencies (rest of the navigation findings)

Still open: a way to record that one leaf needs another first (an optional 'after' link), so agents stop inferring order from prose. Result (2026-11-06): node_dependencies table and the add_dependency MCP tool; focus_node shows needs and needed_by; leaves with an open dependency are left out of next_tasks and the Actions view; loops refused.

title: Configure Supabase
description: Set up the backend: one Supabase project with the auth providers you use enabled, its Site URL set to the app's primary origin, and its URL and publishable key available as VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (local .env, plus the hosting build variables for main and for previews). Before the app has real users, isolate staging from production with a Supabase Branching staging branch or a second project (documentation/DOC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS.md § Staging backend). Your coding agent lists the exact requirements, checks the result, and tells you what only you can do. For Google sign-in, requirements are in documentation/DOC_SUPABASE_GOOGLE_OAUTH.md. If you explicitly say this app does not use Supabase, Google sign-in, anonymous sessions, or error reporting, the agent offers to delete that code. Agent gate: .agents/skills/loop-backlog/references/onboarding.md § Shipped integrations and § Configuration tasks gate (Supabase). Status (2026-11-04): the owner chose the existing Inventhor website project (ref kyzhhofupypwmfjpbyfc, org T-supabase), shared with the inventhor.com website; the Point At migration is applied there. Still open: VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY in .env and hosting build variables, auth providers and URL settings, and the harness signals migration (20261024081200_signals_tables.sql), which is NOT applied to that project. Status (2026-11-06): URL and publishable key are set as Cloudflare build variables. Still open: Supabase Auth redirect URLs for the Point At origins (add only; the project Site URL belongs to the inventhor.com website and must not change), local .env. Result (2026-11-06): the owner added the Point At origins to the project's Auth redirect URLs (Site URL stays the inventhor.com website's) and signed in on the live site at https://fractal-tasks.tom-fab.workers.dev. Local .env is optional for this cloud-only setup.

Web view https://fractal-tasks.tom-fab.workers.dev, MCP server on the point-at Edge Function (token-guarded), tree schema in the Inventhor website project; first tests run and fixed.
